topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Causation and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course scope, learning objectives, and primary themes concerning environmental and biological causes of cancer.

topics.label: Fundamental Concepts, Etiology, and Epidemiology of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the nature of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease while examining how endogenous errors, genetics, and environmental exposures contribute across populations.

topics.label: Infectious, Physical, and Chemical Carcinogenic Agents
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe specific pathogens, radiation, and chemical xenobiotics alongside the biological and metabolic mechanisms through which they induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze how non-mutagenic promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental tissue states facilitate the outgrowth of mutated cells.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer risk.
